about.title: Atherton Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Atherton is a quiet, low-traffic community in San Mateo County, but defective products don't respect a town's size or crash counts. A faulty appliance, a car part that fails on El Camino Real, a tool that malfunctions in a home workshop, or a child's toy with a hidden hazard can cause serious harm regardless of where it happens. California law generally allows injured people to pursue strict liability claims against manufacturers, distributors, and retailers without having to prove negligence — only that the product was defective and that the defect caused the injury. That's a meaningfully different standard than most personal injury cases, and it can open up more than one potentially responsible party. If a defective product has hurt you or someone in your family in Atherton, LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney who understands product liability law and can evaluate what happened, at no cost to you unless there's a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why This Matters for Your Claim

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Proof
items.desc: Because California generally applies strict liability to defective products, you often don't need to show the manufacturer was careless — just that the product was defective and caused your injury.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which may give an attorney more than one avenue to pursue on your behalf.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: Keeping the defective product, its packaging, and any related materials intact can be critical evidence, and an attorney can advise on how to protect it properly.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability claims often rely on strict liability, meaning you generally need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, not that anyone acted carelessly. An independent attorney can review the specifics of your situation to determine which legal theory fits best.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me?
items.answer: Try to preserve it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, including any packaging, instructions, or receipts. Avoid repairing or discarding it, since it may serve as key evidence. An attorney can advise on proper storage or handling before any claim moves forward.

items.question: Does it matter that Atherton doesn't see much traffic-related injury data?
items.answer: No — product liability claims aren't tied to local crash statistics the way vehicle accident cases are. A defective product can cause injury in a home, business, or vehicle anywhere in Atherton or San Mateo County regardless of local traffic patterns. What matters is the product itself and how the injury occurred.

items.question: How much does it cost to get connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing upfront. LawProactive is a free service, and attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
